# F6: weather, lighting and the world state {#sec-fg-weather-lighting}

The engine owns the weather, the sun, the sky and the light. A mod reads
the weather state and re-declares the world lighting at load. This page
states which levers AEE moves, which levers are read only, and what a
wrong value shows.

## What works

- The engine weather commands cover the atmosphere state. `overcast` runs
  0 to 1 from clear to full cloud. `rain` needs an overcast of at least
  0.5 in Arma 3. `fog` uses `setFog [time, fog]`. `wind` is the horizontal
  vector in metres per second and `windStr` is the strength 0 to 1.
  {src:cmd:overcast}
- `setTimeMultiplier` moves the world clock. The engine clamps the value
  to 0.1 to 120. The effect is global. {src:cmd:setTimeMultiplier}
- `waves` is the sea state. The command is read only. The value comes from
  the world config `Weather >> Overcast` bands and the `startWaves` field.
  `setWaves` needs Manual Override in the Eden intel section.
  {src:cfg:CfgWorlds.Weather.Overcast}
- `CfgWorlds` holds the world lighting. The engine core declares
  `DefaultLighting` at `config.cpp:14346`. {src:pbo:Dta/bin.pbo:14346}
- `DefaultLighting >> starEmissivity` is the star draw scale. The engine
  declares `0.3` at `config.cpp:14353`. A world that sets its own value
  shadows the default. {src:pbo:Dta/bin.pbo:14353}
- The world re-opens the default as `class Lighting: DefaultLighting {}`
  at `config.cpp:14435`, so the engine merges instead of replacing.
  {src:pbo:Dta/bin.pbo:14435}
- `DayLightingBrightAlmost` at `config.cpp:14436` and `DayLightingRainy`
  at `config.cpp:14447` carry the night endpoints. The engine
  interpolates the world lighting between them as the sun and moon move.
  {src:pbo:Dta/bin.pbo:14436}
- The `Weather >> Overcast` bands are a ladder. `class Overcast` at
  `config.cpp:14500` holds `Weather1` at overcast 0 through `Weather5` at
  overcast 1. Each band sets `lightingOvercast` 0 to 1 and `waves` 0.15
  to 0.70. {src:cfg:CfgWorlds.Weather.Overcast}
- `CfgLights` at `config.cpp:3466` holds the two engine light classes,
  `ObjectDestructionLight` and `ExplosionLight`. Each carries `color[]`,
  `ambient[]` and `brightness[]`. {src:pbo:Dta/bin.pbo:3466}
- The engine clamps a light with an `Attenuation` block. The core declares
  one on `DefaultLighting >> ThunderBoltLight` at `config.cpp:14358`,
  with `start`, `constant`, `linear` and `quadratic`.
  {src:cfg:CfgLights.Attenuation}
- AEE re-homes the lighting anchor into `CAWorld` and each stock world
  with the explicit base form `class X: X`. The engine merges the values
  through the world class chain. {src:script:addons/lighting/config.cpp}
- AEE sets `starEmissivity` to 25, the vanilla world value. It restores 25
  from an earlier 40, which doubled the vanilla draw with no source.
  {src:script:addons/lighting/config.cpp}

## What does not work

- A script cannot change the tone curve at run time. `HDRNewPars` at
  `config.cpp:14869` is the engine HDR pipeline, and the engine reads it
  at world load. {src:pbo:Dta/bin.pbo:14869}
- A mod cannot add a per-object light at run time. The engine loads the
  light list once, and `CfgLights` declares two classes only.
  {src:cfg:CfgLights}
- A client cannot write the engine weather directly. A client
  `setOvercast`, `setRain` or `setFog` is local and temporary, and the
  value reverts to the server value. {src:cmd:setOvercast}
- AEE does not write engine weather. It reads `overcast`, `rain`, `fog`
  and `wind`, and another mod owns the server write. A push back would
  feed the AEE wind model, which reads the engine wind each tick, and the
  change would compound. {src:adr:ADR-041}
- A re-open that drops its parent empties the class. A file-root
  declaration makes the engine log a missing definition and re-parent
  every world onto an empty class. That empties the tone curve.
  {src:script:addons/lighting/config.cpp}

## Limitations

- The light list loads once. A new light class needs a PBO load, not a
  script call. {src:cfg:CfgLights}
- The world lighting is read at load. `HDRNewPars`, `DOFPars`, `Lighting`,
  the `DayLighting` keyframes and the `Weather` bands are fixed at world
  load. {src:cfg:CfgWorlds}
- The overcast transitions run on the engine clock. `nextWeatherChange`
  states the seconds left in a transition. After it the engine starts a
  new random change over at least 90 minutes. {src:cmd:nextWeatherChange}
- `setTimeMultiplier` is global and clamped to 0.1 to 120. A client cannot
  hold a private rate. {src:cmd:setTimeMultiplier}
- The engine owns the sky, the waves and the tone curve. AEE sets a
  colour, a scale and a band. It cannot move the engine geometry.
  {src:adr:ADR-008}
- A custom world keeps its own values. AEE compensates at run time
  through `fnc_applyWorldLighting`, once per environment tick, and
  publishes the profile as `aee_lighting_worldLighting`.
  {src:script:addons/lighting/config.cpp}

## Breaks visually

- A lighting keyframe that fights the AEE grade breaks the picture. AEE
  keeps the vanilla tone curve and adds a gated `ColorCorrections` grade.
  A world that re-authors the curve away from the vanilla floor doubles
  the change and crushes or lifts the frame. {src:cfg:CfgWorlds.DayLighting}
- An over-bright `starEmissivity` flattens the night sky. AEE carried 40,
  which is 1.6 times the vanilla 25. The star draw doubled with no source.
  {src:script:addons/lighting/config.cpp}
- An attenuation that clips shows a bright disc. A `quadratic` term with
  `start` 0 makes the light fall off fast. A fire or an explosion then
  shows a hard edge, not a glow. {src:cfg:CfgLights.Attenuation}
- A `DayLighting` keyframe below the vanilla floor makes midnight too
  dark. The `deepNight` triplet 0.005, 0.01, 0.01 is the floor. A value
  near zero hides the ground. {src:pbo:Dta/bin.pbo:14436}
- An overcast band that disagrees with the sea state shows flat water.
  The band sets `waves` 0.15 to 0.70. A `Weather5` sky with a calm
  `waves` value shows a heavy sky over a still sea.
  {src:cfg:CfgWorlds.Weather.Overcast}
